cards.subtitle: Deterministic Arthur Schuster (1905) & Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar (1950) conservative two-stream radiative transfer law (R(u) = u/(1+u), T(u) = 1/(1+u) where scaled transport optical depth u = 0.5*(1 - g)*tau in [0.0000, 1.0000], locking total conservative cloud slab flux at R + T = 1.0000x across all 17 stations with 0/17 violated stations) versus naive uncoupled first-order backscatter addition (adding R_1 = u without self-consistently attenuating transmitted flux by 1/(1+u), which inflates total slab energy as 1 + u to 1.2500x at u=0.25, 1.5000x at u=0.50, and 2.0000x at u=1.00 across 16/17 stations) and 64-layer Redheffer star-product adding-doubling cascade.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Volumetric cumulus cloud decks, snowpacks, milk, and translucent foliar canopies with high single-scattering albedo (omega_0 -> 1)
Silver-lining and bright cloud-base diffuse transmittance T = 1 / (1 + 0.5*(1 - g)*tau) where Beer-Lambert exp(-tau) under-predicts brightness
Coupled upward/downward atmospheric irradiance solvers guaranteeing R(u) + T(u) === 1.0000
Closed-form Redheffer star-product slab composition without 64-layer raymarching loops
not_for: Purely absorbing black soot media with zero scattering albedo (omega_0 = 0, where pure Beer-Lambert exp(-tau) applies)
